analysis: The PR changes documentation only: docs/developer/test.md adds a 'Prompt Preparation And Admission' test section (head lines 322-345 per file_changes; I saw only the later head excerpts, units 6 and 7, which are unchanged context). docs/provider/cli-reference.md bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds a `--prompt-prep` row to the benchmark table (head line 572). No executable code, auth, attestation, encryption, cache storage or wire-protocol behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The documented `darkbloom benchmark --prompt-prep` is described as CPU-only: it loads only the tokenizer, uses no network or coordinator, and prints JSON. I looked at it against T-041 (prefix cache) and A-001, because it touches prompt token caching. The docs say the 'prompt token cache's background comparisons' are turned off for the benchmark, and use synthetic conversations. This does not alter the SSD prefix-cache posture (HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, account-scoped salt). The new prompt token cache (PromptTokenCacheTests) is a separate in-process cache, but its implementation is not in the supplied evidence. It was not reviewed for cross-tenant sharing or timing leakage, nor for how plaintext prompt token IDs are retained in memory (T-011/T-014/T-041 class). If the code PR introduces such a cache, the threat model may need an entry covering its scoping to account, model and salt. That is a question for the code-bearing units, not a finding here. The test docs mention `PROMPT_TOKEN_CACHE_MODEL_DIRS`, which reads local model directories in tests only, and the supplied text shows no production surface. The base version of cli-reference.md (unit 2) was only partly supplied (lines 1-404), but the patch is complete. No regression is identified from the documentation changes themselves.
